Fact.Name: Had rental real estate or royalty income (Schedule E Part I)
Fact.Description: Interview gate. Schedule E instructions (2026 draft) printed p. 2 (PDF p. 3): "Use Schedule E (Form 1040) to report income or loss from rental real estate, royalties, ...". Gross income: 26 U.S.C. 61(a)(5), (a)(6).

Fact.Name: Has Schedule E Part I income
Fact.Description: True only when the gate is answered yes; false while unanswered so existing returns are unaffected.

Fact.Name: Rents received (Schedule E line 3, all properties)
Fact.Description: Instructions (2026 draft) printed p. 6 (PDF p. 7), Line 3: "If you received rental income from real estate (including personal property leased with real estate), report the income on line 3." 26 U.S.C. 61(a)(5).

Fact.Name: Rents received (Schedule E line 3, all properties) (derived)
Fact.Description: Rents received (Schedule E line 3, all properties), defaulting to $0 while unanswered so sums stay computable.

Fact.Name: Royalties received (Schedule E line 4, all properties)
Fact.Description: Instructions (2026 draft) printed p. 7 (PDF p. 8), Line 4: "Report on line 4 royalties from oil, gas, or mineral properties (not including operating interests); copyrights; ... and patents." 26 U.S.C. 61(a)(6).

Fact.Name: Royalties received (Schedule E line 4, all properties) (derived)
Fact.Description: Royalties received (Schedule E line 4, all properties), defaulting to $0 while unanswered so sums stay computable.

Fact.Name: Total expenses excluding depreciation (Schedule E lines 5-17 and 19, all properties)
Fact.Description: Schedule E line 20 total expenses, with line 18 (depreciation or depletion) always $0 in this slice because any depreciation is knocked out. Deductibility: 26 U.S.C. 212 (ordinary and necessary expenses for the production or collection of income / management of property held for the production of income).

Fact.Name: Total expenses excluding depreciation (Schedule E lines 5-17 and 19, all properties) (derived)
Fact.Description: Total expenses excluding depreciation (Schedule E lines 5-17 and 19, all properties), defaulting to $0 while unanswered so sums stay computable.

Fact.Name: Any single Part I property had a loss
Fact.Description: Asked because a loss on one property can be hidden by profit on another in the totals. Instructions (2026 draft) printed p. 9 (PDF p. 10), Line 22: "If you have a rental real estate loss from a passive activity (defined earlier), the amount of loss you can deduct may be limited by the passive activity loss rules. You may need to complete Form 8582". 26 U.S.C. 469; at-risk 465 (Line 21: "use Form 6198"); excess business loss 461(l) (Form 461).

Fact.Name: Claims depreciation, amortization, depletion, or vehicle expenses
Fact.Description: Instructions (2026 draft) printed p. 9 (PDF p. 10), Line 18: "See the Instructions for Form 4562 to figure the amount of depreciation to enter on line 18." Printed p. 8 (PDF p. 9): "If you claim any auto expenses (actual or the standard mileage rate), you must complete Part V of Form 4562". Form 4562 is not supported, so the TY2026 mileage rates (72.5 / 76 cents) and section 179 limits ($2,560,000 / $4,090,000) on printed p. 1 are not used.

Fact.Name: Any personal-use days at a rental dwelling unit
Fact.Description: Instructions (2026 draft) printed p. 6 (PDF p. 7), Line 2: "If you rented out a dwelling unit that you also used for personal purposes during the year, you may not be able to deduct all the expenses for the rental part." 26 U.S.C. 280A(c)(5), (e): expense allocation / limits when the unit is used as a residence: https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/280A

Fact.Name: Provides substantial services to renters (cleaning, linens, maid service)
Fact.Description: Instructions for Schedule E (2026 draft) printed p. 7 (PDF p. 8), Line 3: "Generally, rental real estate activity is reported on Schedule E even if it is also a trade or business activity; however, if you provided significant services to the renter, such as maid service, report the rental activity on Schedule C, not on Schedule E. Significant services do not include the furnishing of heat and light, cleaning of public areas, trash collection, or similar services." On Schedule C the profit can be subject to self-employment tax (26 U.S.C. 1401). 26 U.S.C. 1402(a)(1) excludes "rentals from real estate" from net earnings from self-employment; the Schedule C routing above is what takes substantial-service rentals out of that exclusion, so reporting the profit here with $0 SE tax could understate tax.

Fact.Name: Has partnership, S corporation, estate, or trust income (Schedule E Parts II and III)
Fact.Description: #232 and #238. Asked of every filer, not only after a yes to rental or royalty income (/hasScheduleEIncome). 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule E (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/i1040se--dft.pdf, SHA-256 71d19faaf741cf3c), PDF p. 11, Part II: "If you are a member of a partnership or joint venture or a shareholder in an S corporation, use Part II to report your share of the partnership or S corporation income (even if not received) or loss." PDF p. 14, Part III: "If you are a beneficiary of an estate or trust, use Part III to report your part of the income (even if not received) or loss." 26 U.S.C. 702(a) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/702), 1366(a) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/1366), 652(a) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/652), 662(a) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/662). A yes is the gate for Part II. The supported path (ordinary nonpassive box 1 only) is computed on line 32. A loss, passive activity, foreign partnership, PTP, column (e) or (f), any amount other than box 1, Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) box 14 code A, a QBI statement (box 20 code Z or box 17 code V), or line 27 stops the return. Part III is computed only on its supported path. A residual interest in a REMIC is not this question. Schedule Q (Form 1066) is /scheduleEHasPartIVIncome, asked even when this answer is no. See /flowKnockoutScheduleEPartII.

Fact.Name: Any Part I rental is a trade or business (26 U.S.C. 199A)
Fact.Description: #185: a rental that is a trade or business produces qualified business income for the 26 U.S.C. 199A deduction (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/199A). 26 CFR 1.199A-1(b)(14) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/26/1.199A-1): "Trade or business means a trade or business that is a trade or business under section 162 (a section 162 trade or business) other than the trade or business of performing services as an employee. In addition, rental or licensing of tangible or intangible property (rental activity) that does not rise to the level of a section 162 trade or business is nevertheless treated as a trade or business for purposes of section 199A, if the property is rented or licensed to a trade or business conducted by the individual or an RPE which is commonly controlled". Rev. Proc. 2019-38 (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-drop/rp-19-38.pdf) gives a safe harbor for a rental real estate enterprise with 250 or more hours of rental services a year.

Fact.Name: Schedule E Part I total income or (loss) (line 26 / line 41 to Schedule 1 line 5)
Fact.Description: Line 21 per property = (line 3 rents and/or line 4 royalties) - line 20 total expenses; line 26 combines them. Schedule E (2026) draft p. 1, line 21: "Subtract line 20 from line 3 (rents) and/or 4 (royalties)"; line 26: "Total rental real estate and royalty income or (loss). ... Schedule 1 (Form 1040), line 5." Because every loss is knocked out, lines 22 and 25 (passive-loss limits) are always zero here. $0 when the gate is unanswered or no.

Fact.Name: Knockout: Schedule E rental or royalty loss
Fact.Description: Any net loss (total or on any one property) is unsupported: passive activity loss limits (26 U.S.C. 469, Form 8582), at-risk limits (26 U.S.C. 465, Form 6198), and excess business loss (26 U.S.C. 461(l), Form 461). Cites on /scheduleEAnyPropertyLoss.

Fact.Name: Knockout: Schedule E depreciation or vehicle expenses (Form 4562)
Fact.Description: Form 4562 is not supported. Cites on /scheduleEHasDepreciation.

Fact.Name: Knockout: personal use of a rental dwelling unit (IRC 280A)
Fact.Description: Expense allocation under 26 U.S.C. 280A is not supported. Cites on /scheduleEHasPersonalUse.

Fact.Name: Knockout: rental with substantial services (belongs on Schedule C with SE tax)
Fact.Description: Belongs on Schedule C and is subject to SE tax, not Schedule E. Cites on /scheduleEProvidesSubstantialServices.

Fact.Name: Schedule E line 28 column (b) entity type
Fact.Description: Schedule E (2026) draft (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/f1040se--dft.pdf, SHA-256 0bee231f1ecb2470), PDF p. 3, line 28 column (b): "Enter P for partnership; S for S corporation."

Fact.Name: Schedule K-1 entities reported on Schedule E line 28
Fact.Description: One row per partnership or S corporation. 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule E (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/i1040se--dft.pdf, SHA-256 71d19faaf741cf3c), PDF p. 11: "If you are a member of a partnership or joint venture or a shareholder in an S corporation, use Part II to report your share of the partnership or S corporation income (even if not received) or loss." 26 U.S.C. 702(a) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/702) and 1366(a) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/1366). More than four entities are summed into lines 29a, 30, and 32; line 28A is the first entity only. The 2026 draft instructions, PDF p. 9, say to attach a continuation sheet when Part II needs more space.

Fact.Name: Schedule K-1 entity list done
Fact.Description: Filer finished the Schedule E Part II entity loop.

Fact.Name: Schedule E line 27: prior-year unallowed loss or unreimbursed partnership expenses
Fact.Description: Schedule E (2026) draft, PDF p. 3, line 27: "Are you reporting any loss not allowed in a prior year due to the at-risk or basis limitations, a prior-year unallowed loss from a passive activity (if that loss was not reported on Form 8582), or unreimbursed partnership expenses?" A yes needs Form 8582, Form 6198, or the basis computation, none of which are computed here, so it stops the return (/flowKnockoutScheduleEPartIILine27).

Fact.Name: Has estate or trust income (Schedule E Part III)
Fact.Description: 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule E, PDF p. 14: "If you are a beneficiary of an estate or trust, use Part III to report your part of the income (even if not received) or loss. You should receive a Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) from the fiduciary." 26 U.S.C. 652(a) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/652) and 662(a) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/662). A yes opens the Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) interview. The supported path is computed on line 37. A loss, passive activity, box 5, box 7, box 8, any other box, a foreign trust, Form 8082, a basis limit, an at-risk limit, or a passive deduction stops the return. See /flowKnockoutScheduleEPartIII.

Fact.Name: Has residual interest in a REMIC (Schedule E Part IV)
Fact.Description: 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule E, PDF p. 14: "If you are the holder of a residual interest in a REMIC, use Part IV to report your total share of the REMIC's taxable income or loss for each quarter included in your tax year. You should receive Schedule Q (Form 1066) and instructions from the REMIC for each quarter." Asked of every filer, including a filer who answered /scheduleEHasPartIIIncome no. 26 U.S.C. 860C (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/860C). Part IV is not computed. A yes stops the return, and line 39 stays incomplete so the REMIC amount is not entered as zero. An unanswered question leaves /flowKnockoutScheduleEPartIV incomplete, so the print is refused.

Fact.Name: Partnership or S corporation name (line 28 column (a))
Fact.Description: Schedule E (2026) draft, PDF p. 3, line 28 column (a): "(a) Name".

Fact.Name: Entity type (line 28 column (b))
Fact.Description: Schedule E (2026) draft, PDF p. 3, line 28 column (b): "Enter P for partnership; S for S corporation."

Fact.Name: Foreign partnership (line 28 column (c))
Fact.Description: Schedule E (2026) draft, PDF p. 3, line 28 column (c): "Check if foreign partnership". A checked box is out of scope (/flowKnockoutScheduleEPartIIForeignOrPtp).

Fact.Name: Publicly traded partnership
Fact.Description: 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule E, PDF p. 12: "See the Schedule K-1 instructions before entering on your return other partnership items from a passive activity or income or loss from any publicly traded partnership." A PTP is out of scope. 26 U.S.C. 469(k) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/469) limits the passive loss from a publicly traded partnership, and 26 U.S.C. 199A(b)(1)(B) treats qualified PTP income separately from qualified business income.

Fact.Name: Partnership or S corporation trades in financial instruments or commodities
Fact.Description: 26 U.S.C. 1411(c)(2) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/1411) treats as a section 1411 trade or business "(A) a passive activity (within the meaning of section 469) with respect to the taxpayer, or (B) a trade or business of trading in financial instruments or commodities (as defined in section 475(e)(2))." Material-participation ordinary income that is not a trading business is not net investment income, so it is not added to Form 8960 line 4a. A trading business would be, and Form 8960 does not take it from Part II, so a yes stops the return.

Fact.Name: Schedule K-1 box 1 ordinary business income (loss)
Fact.Description: Partner's Instructions for Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) (2025) (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1065sk1.pdf, SHA-256 659063e0aaa36e44), box 1, ordinary business income (loss). Shareholder's Instructions for Schedule K-1 (Form 1120-S) report the same ordinary business income (loss) in box 1. 26 U.S.C. 702(a)(8) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/702): a partner takes into account "taxable income or loss ... exclusive of items requiring separate computation". 26 U.S.C. 1366(a)(1) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/1366) is the S corporation counterpart. 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule E, PDF p. 13: "enter in the applicable column of line 28 your current-year ordinary income or loss ... from the partnership or S corporation." A negative amount is a loss and stops the return. No minimum: the loss knockout needs the signed amount.

Fact.Name: Material participation in this partnership or S corporation
Fact.Description: 26 U.S.C. 469(h)(1) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/469): a taxpayer materially participates when involved in the operations of the activity "on a regular, continuous, and substantial basis." 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule E, PDF pp. 11-12: "If you have passive activity income, complete column (h) of Part II, for that activity. If you have nonpassive income or losses, complete columns (i) through (k) of Part II, as appropriate." Yes puts nonnegative box 1 in column (k). No is passive and stops the return (column (h) is not filed in this slice).

Fact.Name: Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) box 14 code A net earnings from self-employment
Fact.Description: 2026 draft Schedule SE (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/f1040sse--dft.pdf, SHA-256 a59fa5dcf2f0a8a5a71c46aa3837e9e8e605eeecc0a666bcb784a368900d141c), PDF p. 2, line 2: "Net profit or (loss) from Schedule C, line 31; and Schedule K-1 (Form 1065), box 14, code A (other than farming)." 26 U.S.C. 1402(a) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/1402). 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule E, PDF p. 12: "Enter the amount from box 14, code A, of Schedule K-1 (Form 1065), on Schedule SE after you reduce this amount by any allowable expenses attributable to that income." PDF p. 13: "Your share of the net income of an S corporation is not subject to self-employment tax." A nonzero amount is not added to Schedule SE line 2; it stops the return. Enter zero when box 14 code A is blank, including every S corporation.

Fact.Name: Schedule K-1 has a section 199A statement (box 20 code Z or box 17 code V)
Fact.Description: 26 U.S.C. 199A(c) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/199A) qualified business income from a partnership or S corporation is reported on a statement: Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) box 20 code Z, or Schedule K-1 (Form 1120-S) box 17 code V. Form 8995 lines 6-9 are not filled from box 1. A statement means there is an amount to enter, so the return stops. Blank or zero leaves nothing to enter.

Fact.Name: Any Schedule K-1 amount other than box 1
Fact.Description: Any box other than box 1 ordinary business income (loss), including guaranteed payments, interest, dividends, royalties, section 179, credits, and other separately stated items. 26 U.S.C. 702(a)(1)-(7) and 1366(a)(1)(A) require those items to be taken into account separately. They are not entered on Schedule E line 28 column (k) in this slice, so any such amount stops the return. Answer no only when every other box is blank or zero.

Fact.Name: Line 28 column (e): basis computation required
Fact.Description: Schedule E (2026) draft, PDF p. 3: "If you report a loss, receive a distribution, dispose of stock, or receive a loan repayment from an S corporation, you must check the box in column (e) on line 28 and attach the required basis computation." 26 U.S.C. 1366(d)(1) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/1366) and 1367 (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/1367). A checked box stops the return. Answer no when there is no S corporation distribution, stock disposition, or loan repayment.

Fact.Name: Line 28 column (f): any amount is not at risk
Fact.Description: Schedule E (2026) draft, PDF p. 3: "If you report a loss from an at-risk activity for which any amount is not at risk, you must check the box in column (f) on line 28 and attach Form 6198." 26 U.S.C. 465(a)(1) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/465). A checked box stops the return.

Fact.Name: Box 1 is a loss
Fact.Description: Box 1 less than zero. 26 U.S.C. 469(a)(1), 465(a)(1), 704(d)(1) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/704), 1366(d)(1), and 461(l) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/461) can limit a loss. None of those forms are computed here.

Fact.Name: Does not materially participate
Box 14 code A is not zero
Foreign partnership or publicly traded partnership
Line 28 column (k) nonpassive income
Fact.Description: Schedule E (2026) draft, PDF p. 3, column (k): "Nonpassive income from Schedule K-1". 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule E, PDF pp. 11-12: nonpassive income goes in columns (i) through (k). Column (k) is box 1, rounded to whole dollars, when the filer materially participates and box 1 is zero or positive. 26 U.S.C. 6102(a) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/6102): "the fractional part of a dollar shall be disregarded unless it amounts to one-half dollar or more, in which case it shall be increased to one dollar." Passive income and losses are not entered here; those returns stop.

Fact.Name: Line 28 column (h) passive income
Fact.Description: Schedule E (2026) draft, PDF p. 3, column (h): "Passive income from Schedule K-1". Used only so line 30 can add columns (h) and (k) when the activity is passive. A passive activity stops the return before filing, so a submitted return has column (h) at zero.

Fact.Name: This K-1 is in the supported Part II slice
Fact.Description: Domestic partnership or S corporation, column (c) unchecked, not a PTP, not a trading business, box 1 at least zero, box 14 code A zero, no section 199A statement, no other K-1 amount, column (e) and column (f) unchecked, and material participation yes.

Fact.Name: Schedule K-1 entity interview complete
Fact.Description: Every Part II question for this entity has an answer.

Fact.Name: Schedule E line 28A entity
Fact.Description: The first partnership or S corporation on line 28. Schedule E (2026) draft, PDF p. 3, row A.

Fact.Name: Schedule E line 28A column (k)
Fact.Description: Nonpassive income on line 28A. Same amount as that entity's box 1 when the supported path applies. Cite on /scheduleEK1s/*/columnK.

Fact.Name: Schedule E line 29a column (k)
Fact.Description: Schedule E (2026) draft, PDF p. 3, line 29a: "Totals" of the income columns. Column (k) is the sum of line 28 column (k). $0 when the K-1 question is unanswered or no, so the rest of the return still computes. Also $0 when the partnership list is finished and empty and Part III is yes, so a trust-only return does not leave line 32 incomplete. Incomplete when the filer answered yes, has not finished an empty list or a Part III interview, or a column (k) amount is still unanswered, so line 32 is not filed as zero.

Fact.Name: Schedule E line 29a column (h)
Fact.Description: Sum of line 28 column (h). On a return that can be filed this is zero: passive income stops the return. Same completeness rule as column (k).

Fact.Name: Schedule E line 30
Fact.Description: Schedule E (2026) draft, PDF p. 3, line 30: "Add columns (h) and (k) of line 29a." Whole dollars, 26 U.S.C. 6102(a).

Fact.Name: Schedule E line 31
Fact.Description: Schedule E (2026) draft, PDF p. 3, line 31: "Add columns (g), (i), and (j) of line 29b." This slice does not compute a loss or a section 179 deduction, so line 31 is zero whenever line 30 is complete, and incomplete when line 30 is incomplete.

Fact.Name: Schedule E line 32
Fact.Description: Schedule E (2026) draft, PDF p. 3, line 32: "Total partnership and S corporation income or (loss). Combine lines 30 and 31." Whole dollars, 26 U.S.C. 6102(a).

Fact.Name: Schedule E line 41
Fact.Description: Schedule E (2026) draft, PDF p. 4, line 41: "Total income or (loss). Combine lines 26, 32, 37, 39, and 40. Enter the result here and on Schedule 1 (Form 1040), line 5." Line 26 is /scheduleENetIncome. Line 32 is /scheduleEPartIILine32. Line 37 is /scheduleEPartIIILine37. Line 39 is /scheduleEPartIVLine39: $0 when Part IV is no, and incomplete when Part IV is yes so a REMIC is not entered as zero. Line 40 (Form 4835) is not collected. Whole dollars, 26 U.S.C. 6102(a). 26 U.S.C. 61(a), 702(a), 1366(a), 652(a), 662(a).

Fact.Name: Answered yes to Schedule K-1 income
Fact.Description: True only when /scheduleEHasPartIIIncome is answered yes. Unanswered is false, so Schedule 1 is not required solely because the question has not been reached. The print still refuses while the question is unanswered (/flowKnockoutScheduleEPartII).

Fact.Name: Knockout: Schedule K-1 ordinary loss
Fact.Description: Any box 1 loss. 26 U.S.C. 469(a)(1) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/469) disallows the passive activity loss. 26 U.S.C. 465(a)(1) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/465) limits a loss to the amount at risk (Form 6198). 26 U.S.C. 704(d)(1) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/704) and 1366(d)(1) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/1366) limit a loss to basis. 26 U.S.C. 461(l) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/461) is the excess business loss (Form 461). Complete false when /scheduleEHasPartIIIncome is false.

Fact.Name: Knockout: passive partnership or S corporation (no material participation)
Fact.Description: 26 U.S.C. 469(c)(1) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/469): a passive activity is a trade or business in which the taxpayer does not materially participate. Column (h) and section 1411 net investment income are not computed for that activity. Complete false when /scheduleEHasPartIIIncome is false.

Fact.Name: Knockout: Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) box 14 code A
Fact.Description: A nonzero box 14 code A belongs on Schedule SE line 1a or line 2 and is not added there. Cites on /scheduleEK1s/*/box14CodeA. Complete false when /scheduleEHasPartIIIncome is false.

Fact.Name: Knockout: Schedule K-1 section 199A statement
Fact.Description: Box 20 code Z or box 17 code V is qualified business income that Form 8995 does not take from this K-1. Cites on /scheduleEK1s/*/hasQbiStatement. Complete false when /scheduleEHasPartIIIncome is false.

Fact.Name: Knockout: Schedule K-1 amount other than box 1
Fact.Description: Any separately stated K-1 amount. Cites on /scheduleEK1s/*/hasOtherK1Amount. Complete false when /scheduleEHasPartIIIncome is false.

Fact.Name: Knockout: Schedule E line 28 column (e)
Fact.Description: S corporation distribution, stock disposition, loan repayment, or other required basis computation. Cites on /scheduleEK1s/*/basisComputationRequired. Complete false when /scheduleEHasPartIIIncome is false.

Fact.Name: Knockout: Schedule E line 28 column (f)
Fact.Description: Any amount not at risk (Form 6198). Cites on /scheduleEK1s/*/anyAmountNotAtRisk. Complete false when /scheduleEHasPartIIIncome is false.

Fact.Name: Knockout: foreign partnership or publicly traded partnership
Fact.Description: Column (c) or a publicly traded partnership. Cites on /scheduleEK1s/*/isForeignPartnership and /scheduleEK1s/*/isPubliclyTradedPartnership. Complete false when /scheduleEHasPartIIIncome is false.

Fact.Name: Knockout: trading in financial instruments or commodities
Fact.Description: 26 U.S.C. 1411(c)(2)(B). Cites on /scheduleEK1s/*/isTradingBusiness. The amount is not added to Form 8960 line 4a. Complete false when /scheduleEHasPartIIIncome is false.

Fact.Name: Knockout: Schedule E line 27 yes
Fact.Description: Prior-year unallowed loss or unreimbursed partnership expenses. Cites on /scheduleEPartIILine27. Complete false when /scheduleEHasPartIIIncome is false.

Fact.Name: Estates and trusts reported on Schedule E line 33
Fact.Description: One row per estate or trust. 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule E (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/i1040se--dft.pdf, SHA-256 71d19faaf741cf3c), PDF p. 14: "If you are a beneficiary of an estate or trust, use Part III to report your part of the income (even if not received) or loss. You should receive a Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) from the fiduciary." 26 U.S.C. 652(a) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/652) and 662(a) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/662). More than two estates are summed into lines 34a, 35, and 37. The 2026 draft instructions, PDF p. 10, say to attach a continuation sheet when Part III needs more space.

Fact.Name: Estate and trust list done
Fact.Description: Filer finished the Schedule E Part III estate and trust loop.

Fact.Name: Estate or trust name (line 33 column (a))
Fact.Description: Schedule E (2026) draft, PDF p. 3, line 33 column (a): "(a) Name".

Fact.Name: Foreign beneficiary (Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) item H)
Fact.Description: Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) (2025) (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f1041sk1.pdf, SHA-256 d8d7b6eacabdf145), item H: "Domestic beneficiary" or "Foreign beneficiary". 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule E, PDF p. 14: a foreign trust may require Schedule B Part III and Form 3520. A foreign beneficiary is out of scope.

Fact.Name: Foreign trust
Fact.Description: 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule E, PDF p. 14: "An individual who received a distribution from, or who was the grantor of, or transferor to, a foreign trust must also complete Part III of Schedule B (Form 1040) and may have to file Form 3520." 26 U.S.C. 679 (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/679). A yes stops the return.

Fact.Name: Treating a K-1 item differently from the estate or trust (Form 8082)
Fact.Description: 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule E, PDF p. 14: "If you are treating items on your tax return differently from the way the estate or trust reported them on its return, you may have to file Form 8082." A yes stops the return.

Fact.Name: Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) box 5 other portfolio and nonbusiness income
Fact.Description: Beneficiary's Instructions for Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) (2025) (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1041sk1.pdf, SHA-256 516ed87ce8108a13), Box 5: "The amount reported in this box is your distributive share of royalties, annuities, and other income that isn't subject to the passive activity rules." Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) (2025) page 2: report box 5 on "Schedule E, line 33, column (f)". A nonzero amount is net investment income under 26 U.S.C. 1411(c)(1)(A)(i) or income in respect of a decedent whose character is not modeled, and Form 8960 line 4a does not take it, so it stops the return. No minimum: a loss must remain visible to the loss knockout.

Fact.Name: Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) box 6 ordinary business income
Fact.Description: Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) (2025) page 2: box 6 "Ordinary business income" is reported on "Schedule E, line 33, column (d) or (f)". Beneficiary's Instructions, Boxes 6 Through 8: the fiduciary reports the distributive share of income from each trade or business. 26 U.S.C. 662(a). Material participation puts a nonnegative amount in column (f). A negative amount stops the return.

Fact.Name: Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) box 7 net rental real estate income
Fact.Description: Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) (2025) page 2: box 7 is reported on "Schedule E, line 33, column (d) or (f)". 26 U.S.C. 469(c)(2) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/469): a rental real estate activity is a passive activity. Schedule E (2026) draft, PDF p. 4, line 43 is the real estate professional reconciliation and is not computed. Any nonzero amount stops the return (Form 8582).

Fact.Name: Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) box 8 other rental income
Fact.Description: Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) (2025) page 2: box 8 "Other rental income" is reported on "Schedule E, line 33, column (d) or (f)". 26 U.S.C. 469(c)(2) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/469): the term passive activity includes any rental activity, except as provided in 469(c)(7). 26 U.S.C. 469(c)(4): material participation is not taken into account in determining whether an activity is a rental activity under (c)(2). Box 8 is not 469(c)(7) rental real estate (that exception is box 7, and Schedule E line 43 is not computed). A nonnegative amount is column (d) only. Any nonzero amount stops the return. A negative amount also stops the return.

Fact.Name: Material participation in this estate or trust activity
Fact.Description: 26 U.S.C. 469(h)(1): a taxpayer materially participates when involved "on a regular, continuous, and substantial basis." Yes puts nonnegative box 6 in column (f). Box 8 stays in column (d): 26 U.S.C. 469(c)(2) and 469(c)(4). No is passive (column (d)) and stops the return.

Fact.Name: Any Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) amount other than boxes 5, 6, 7, and 8
Fact.Description: Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) (2025) page 2 sends box 1 to Form 1040 line 2b, box 2a to line 3b, box 2b to line 3a, boxes 3 and 4a to Schedule D, box 9 to Form 8582 or Schedule E columns (c) or (e), box 10 to Schedule A, box 11 to Schedule 1, Schedule A, Schedule D, or Form 6251, box 12 to Form 6251, box 13 to a credit line, and box 14 to other forms, including code I (section 199A) and code H (Form 8960). Those amounts are not entered from this slice. Answer no only when every such box is blank or zero.

Fact.Name: A loss from this estate or trust is limited by basis
Fact.Description: 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule E, PDF p. 4, Limitation on Losses: "Basis rules apply to losses from a partnership or S corporation." Form 7203 is the S corporation stock and debt basis computation under 26 U.S.C. 1366(d) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/1366) and 1367 (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/1367). This tool does not compute a basis limit for a beneficiary of an estate or trust. A yes stops the return instead of treating the limit as zero. Answer no when no basis limit applies.

Fact.Name: Any amount of this estate or trust is not at risk
Fact.Description: 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule E, PDF p. 4: "At-risk rules apply to losses from rental real estate or royalties. They also apply to losses from a partnership, S corporation, estate, or trust." 26 U.S.C. 465(a)(1) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/465). Form 6198 is not computed. A yes stops the return.

Fact.Name: Passive deduction or loss from this estate or trust (Form 8582)
Fact.Description: Schedule E (2026) draft, PDF p. 3, line 33 column (c): "Passive deduction or loss allowed (attach Form 8582 if required)." Column (e) is "Deduction or loss from Schedule K-1". 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule E, PDF p. 4: "Passive activity loss rules apply to losses from rental real estate. They also apply to losses from a partnership, S corporation, estate, or trust." 26 U.S.C. 469(a)(1). A yes stops the return. Answer no when columns (c) and (e) would be blank or zero.

Fact.Name: A Schedule E box on this K-1 is a loss
Fact.Description: Box 5, 6, 7, or 8 less than zero. 26 U.S.C. 469(a)(1) (Form 8582), 465(a)(1) (Form 6198), and 461(l) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/461) (Form 461) can limit a loss. None of those forms are computed here.

Fact.Name: Does not materially participate in this estate or trust
Box 5 is not zero
Box 7 is not zero
Box 8 is not zero
Fact.Description: Other rental income. 26 U.S.C. 469(c)(2) and 469(c)(4). Not 469(c)(7) rental real estate professional income.

Fact.Name: Foreign beneficiary or foreign trust
Line 33 column (f) other income
Fact.Description: Schedule E (2026) draft, PDF p. 3, column (f): "Other income from Schedule K-1". Nonpassive box 6, plus nonnegative box 5, rounded to whole dollars. Box 8 is not included. 26 U.S.C. 469(c)(2) and 469(c)(4) make other rental income passive without regard to material participation, so it is column (d). 26 U.S.C. 6102(a): "the fractional part of a dollar shall be disregarded unless it amounts to one-half dollar or more, in which case it shall be increased to one dollar." A loss leaves this amount incomplete. A filed return has box 5 at zero, so column (f) is box 6.

Fact.Name: Line 33 column (d) passive income
Fact.Description: Schedule E (2026) draft, PDF p. 3, column (d): "Passive income from Schedule K-1". Nonnegative box 7 and box 8 are reported here whether or not the filer materially participates. 26 U.S.C. 469(c)(2) and 469(c)(4). A passive filer also reports nonnegative box 6. A filed return has column (d) at zero because passive income, box 7, and box 8 stop the return.

Fact.Name: This estate or trust is in the supported Part III slice
Fact.Description: Domestic beneficiary, not a foreign trust, no Form 8082, material participation yes, box 5, box 7, and box 8 zero, box 6 at least zero, no other K-1 amount, no basis limit, no amount not at risk, and no passive deduction or loss. Box 8 is a rental activity under 26 U.S.C. 469(c)(2) and 469(c)(4) and is not on the supported path.

Fact.Name: Estate or trust interview complete
Fact.Description: Every Part III question for this estate or trust has an answer.

Fact.Name: Schedule E line 33A estate or trust
Fact.Description: The first estate or trust on line 33. Schedule E (2026) draft, PDF p. 3, row A.

Fact.Name: Schedule E line 33A column (f)
Fact.Description: Other income on line 33A. Cite on /scheduleEEstates/*/columnF.

Fact.Name: Schedule E line 34a column (f)
Fact.Description: Schedule E (2026) draft, PDF p. 3, line 34a: "Totals" of column (f). $0 when the K-1 question or the Part III question is unanswered or no. Incomplete when Part III is yes and no estate or trust is listed, or a column (f) amount is unanswered, so line 37 is not filed as zero.

Fact.Name: Schedule E line 34a column (d)
Fact.Description: Sum of line 33 column (d). On a return that can be filed this is zero. Same completeness rule as column (f).

Fact.Name: Schedule E line 35
Fact.Description: Schedule E (2026) draft, PDF p. 3, line 35: "Add columns (d) and (f) of line 34a." Whole dollars, 26 U.S.C. 6102(a).

Fact.Name: Schedule E line 36
Fact.Description: Schedule E (2026) draft, PDF p. 3, line 36: "Add columns (c) and (e) of line 34b." This slice does not compute a deduction or loss, so line 36 is zero whenever line 35 is complete, and incomplete when line 35 is incomplete.

Fact.Name: Schedule E line 37
Fact.Description: Schedule E (2026) draft, PDF p. 3, line 37: "Total estate and trust income or (loss). Combine lines 35 and 36." Whole dollars, 26 U.S.C. 6102(a). 26 U.S.C. 652(a) and 662(a). $0 when Part III does not apply. Incomplete when Part III is yes and the estate list is empty or a column amount is unanswered.

Fact.Name: Schedule E line 39
Fact.Description: Schedule E (2026) draft, PDF p. 3, line 39: "Combine columns (d) and (e) only. Enter the result here and include in the total on line 41 below." Part IV is not computed. $0 when the filer answered no, and $0 while the question is unanswered so the rest of the return can still be computed. The unanswered question leaves /flowKnockoutScheduleEPartIV incomplete, so the print is refused. Incomplete when the filer answered yes, so a REMIC residual interest is not entered as zero. This does not depend on /scheduleEHasPartIIIncome. 26 U.S.C. 860C. Schedule Q (Form 1066).

Fact.Name: Knockout: Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) loss
Fact.Description: Any box 5, 6, 7, or 8 loss. 26 U.S.C. 469(a)(1) (Form 8582), 465(a)(1) (Form 6198), and 461(l) (Form 461). Complete false when Part III is no.

Fact.Name: Knockout: passive estate or trust (no material participation)
Fact.Description: 26 U.S.C. 469(c)(1) and 469(h)(1). Column (d) is not filed. Complete false when Part III is no.

Fact.Name: Knockout: Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) box 5
Fact.Description: Portfolio or nonbusiness income, including royalties, annuities, and income in respect of a decedent. Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) (2025) page 2 reports it in column (f), and 26 U.S.C. 1411(c)(1)(A)(i) includes royalties and annuities in net investment income. Form 8960 line 4a does not take it. Complete false when Part III is no.

Fact.Name: Knockout: Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) box 7
Fact.Description: Net rental real estate income. 26 U.S.C. 469(c)(2). Form 8582 and Schedule E line 43 are not computed. Complete false when Part III is no.

Fact.Name: Knockout: Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) box 8
Fact.Description: Other rental income. 26 U.S.C. 469(c)(2) includes any rental activity in the term passive activity. 26 U.S.C. 469(c)(4) applies that rule without regard to material participation. Box 8 is not 469(c)(7) rental real estate professional income. A nonzero amount is column (d) and stops the return. Form 8960 line 4a does not take it. Complete false when Part III is no.

Fact.Name: Knockout: Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) amount other than boxes 5 through 8
Fact.Description: Interest, dividends, capital gain, deductions, credits, AMT items, or box 14, including section 199A code I. Cites on /scheduleEEstates/*/hasOtherK1Amount. Complete false when Part III is no.

Fact.Name: Knockout: basis limit on an estate or trust (Form 7203 not computed)
Fact.Description: Form 7203 and 26 U.S.C. 1366(d) limit an S corporation loss. 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule E, PDF p. 4: basis rules apply to partnership and S corporation losses. This tool does not compute a basis limit for a beneficiary. Complete false when Part III is no.

Fact.Name: Knockout: estate or trust amount not at risk (Form 6198)
Fact.Description: 26 U.S.C. 465(a)(1). 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule E, PDF p. 4: at-risk rules apply to a loss from an estate or trust. Form 6198 is not computed. Complete false when Part III is no.

Fact.Name: Knockout: passive deduction or loss from an estate or trust (Form 8582)
Fact.Description: 26 U.S.C. 469(a)(1). Schedule E line 33 columns (c) and (e). Form 8582 is not computed. Complete false when Part III is no.

Fact.Name: Knockout: foreign beneficiary or foreign trust
Fact.Description: 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule E, PDF p. 14, Form 3520 and Schedule B Part III. 26 U.S.C. 679. Complete false when Part III is no.

Fact.Name: Knockout: Form 8082 inconsistent treatment
Fact.Description: 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule E, PDF p. 14: file Form 8082 when items are treated differently from the estate or trust. Complete false when Part III is no.

Fact.Name: Schedule E Part III is out of scope
Fact.Description: True when any Part III knockout is true.

Fact.Name: Schedule E Part III supported path is complete
Fact.Description: The filer answered yes, at least one estate or trust is listed, every row is complete, and every row is supported nonpassive income from box 6. Box 8 is not supported. 26 U.S.C. 469(c)(2) and 469(c)(4).

Fact.Name: Knockout: Schedule E Part III out of scope, or the estate or trust question is unanswered
Fact.Description:
#85. Incomplete while /scheduleEHasPartIIIncome is unanswered, and while that answer is yes and /scheduleEHasPartIIIIncome is unanswered, so the print is refused through /flowKnockoutScheduleEPartII and line 37 is not a silent zero. Complete false when either answer is no, and when every line 33 estate or trust is the supported path. True when /scheduleEPartIIIOutOfScope is true.
Supported path. Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) (2025) page 2: box 6 "Ordinary business income" is reported on "Schedule E, line 33, column (d) or (f)". Material participation (26 U.S.C. 469(h)(1)) puts a nonnegative amount in column (f). Box 8 "Other rental income" is a rental activity. 26 U.S.C. 469(c)(2) includes any rental activity in the term passive activity, and 469(c)(4) applies that rule without regard to material participation. It is not 469(c)(7) rental real estate professional income. A nonnegative box 8 is column (d), and any nonzero box 8 stops the return. 2026 draft Schedule E, PDF p. 3, line 35: "Add columns (d) and (f) of line 34a." Line 37: "Total estate and trust income or (loss). Combine lines 35 and 36." 26 U.S.C. 652(a) and 662(a).
Not net investment income. 26 U.S.C. 1411(c)(2) includes a passive activity. Material-participation box 6 is not added to Form 8960 line 4a. Box 8 is passive under 469(c)(2) and 469(c)(4), is not on line 4a, and stops the return. Box 5 and box 7 stop the return.
Not self-employment. A beneficiary's share of estate or trust income is not entered on Schedule SE. 26 U.S.C. 1402(a). Not qualified business income. Box 14 code I stops the return. Box 6 is not treated as qualified business income on Form 8995.

Fact.Name: Knockout: Schedule E Part IV (REMIC)
Fact.Description: A residual interest in a REMIC is not computed. Schedule Q (Form 1066). Cites on /scheduleEHasPartIVIncome. Incomplete while that question is unanswered, so the print is refused. Complete false when the answer is no. True when the answer is yes, including when /scheduleEHasPartIIIncome is no. 26 U.S.C. 860C.

Fact.Name: Knockout: Part II income and Form 8615
Fact.Description: Form 8615 is not supported. 26 U.S.C. 1(g) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/1) taxes certain children on unearned income. Instructions for Form 8615 (2026 draft), Who Must File, apply when the child does not file a joint return and is under 18, or age 18, or a full-time student under 24. /form8615UnearnedIncome includes Schedule E rents and royalties only (the Form 8615 instructions list "rents, royalties"). Partnership or S corporation ordinary income is not added there. A primary filer under 24 who does not file jointly and has line 32 greater than zero is stopped instead. Line 32 or line 37 greater than zero is tested first, so both at zero is complete false without reading age. Estate or trust income is unearned income under 26 U.S.C. 1(g). Form 8615 is not computed, so that income stops the return instead of being left off the kiddie-tax worksheet. Complete false when there is no Part II or Part III income.

Fact.Name: Schedule E Part II is out of scope
Fact.Description: True when any Part II, Part III, or Part IV knockout is true.

Fact.Name: Schedule E Part II supported path is complete
Fact.Description: The filer answered yes, line 27 is no, and Part IV is no. Every listed partnership or S corporation is supported ordinary nonpassive income. Part III is no, or every estate or trust is the supported path. A trust-only return may finish the partnership list with no entities.

Fact.Name: Schedule K-1 question is resolved for the section
Fact.Description: True when the filer answered no, or the supported path is complete, or an out-of-scope knockout is true. Incomplete while a yes has no finished entity list and no knockout yet.

Fact.Name: Knockout: Schedule E Part II out of scope, or the K-1 question is unanswered
Fact.Description:
#85. The K-1 question is asked of every filer. Incomplete while /scheduleEHasPartIIIncome is unanswered, so the print is refused and /flowIsKnockedOut stays incomplete (no silent zero of K-1 income). A yes to /scheduleEHasPartIVIncome makes this true even when the K-1 answer is no, so a Schedule Q (Form 1066) holder is not filed as zero. Complete false when the K-1 answer is no and Part IV is no, and when the supported Part II path is complete and Part IV is no. Part III may be no, or every estate or trust may be the supported path (line 37, box 6 only). True when any out-of-scope knockout is true. A yes with an empty or unfinished list, or a Part III yes with no finished estate or trust, stays incomplete so lines 32 and 37 are not filed as zero.
Income tax. 2026 draft Schedule E, PDF p. 4, line 41: "Total income or (loss). Combine lines 26, 32, 37, 39, and 40. Enter the result here and on Schedule 1 (Form 1040), line 5." Line 32 is /scheduleEPartIILine32. Line 37 is /scheduleEPartIIILine37. 26 U.S.C. 702(a), 1366(a), 652(a), and 662(a).
Self-employment. A supported return has box 14 code A at zero, so Schedule SE line 2 stays Schedule C only. A nonzero box 14 code A is /flowKnockoutScheduleEPartIIBox14CodeA. 26 U.S.C. 1402(a). 2026 draft Schedule SE, PDF p. 2, line 2 includes that code.
Net investment income. 26 U.S.C. 1411(c)(2) includes a passive activity or trading in financial instruments or commodities. Material-participation box 1 that is not a trading business is not added to Form 8960 line 4a. Passive, trading, PTP, and any other box stop the return.
Qualified business income. A blank box 20 code Z or box 17 code V leaves Form 8995 lines 6-9 at zero. A statement stops the return. Box 1 is not treated as qualified business income.

Fact.Name: Knockout: Schedule E rental treated as a trade or business (QBI not computed)
Fact.Description: #185: a trade-or-business rental needs the 26 U.S.C. 199A deduction on Form 1040 (2026) draft line 13b, "Qualified business income deduction from Form 8995 or Form 8995-A" (PDF p. 3). Line 13b (taxCalculations /qualifiedBusinessIncomeDeduction) is not computed yet, so a "yes" is stopped instead of filing line 13b as $0. Cites on /scheduleERentalIsTradeOrBusiness. Complete false when there is no Part I income (/hasScheduleEIncome false) or the answer is "no"; incomplete while a filer with Part I income has not answered, and /scheduleESectionIsComplete requires the answer.

Fact.Name: Knockout: Schedule E income with the EITC
Fact.Description: 26 U.S.C. 32(i)(2)(C): disqualified income includes "the excess (if any) of— (i) gross income from rents or royalties not derived in the ordinary course of a trade or business, over (ii) the sum of" the allocable deductions. The eitc modules do not include Schedule E in the investment-income test yet, so any nonzero Schedule E result with EITC eligibility is knocked out. https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/32

Fact.Name: Schedule E section complete
Fact.Description: The rental gate, the K-1 question (/scheduleEHasPartIIIncome), and the REMIC question (/scheduleEHasPartIVIncome) are answered. The K-1 question is required even when /hasScheduleEIncome is false (#232, #238). The REMIC question is required even when the K-1 answer is no, so a Schedule Q (Form 1066) holder is not left at line 39 of $0. A yes is not done until the supported Part II path is complete or an out-of-scope knockout is true (/scheduleEPartIIResolved). If the filer has Part I income, every amount and screener is answered too. IsComplete of an unanswered question is false, so an otherwise finished interview stays incomplete until both questions are answered.
